Package com.kristensoft.kdc

Class Agent

  • java.lang.Object
    • com.kristensoft.kdc.Agent
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    Serializable
    Direct Known Subclasses:
    Reply
    public class Agent
extends Object
implements Serializable
    Represents an object that can be transmitted by KDC to a remote receiver.

    An Agent may carry application data and, when configured with a visit method and API class, may be dispatched by the receiver. During dispatch, KDC invokes the agent's visit method and supplies the receiver's implementation of the specified API.

    An agent is considered dispatchable when it is a subclass of Agent and has both a visit method name and API class name. A plain Agent may therefore be used to transport data without invoking receiver-side application logic.

    Each agent is assigned a unique UUID. KDC also maintains runtime information such as the transport protocol, synchronous state, serialized size, and latency measurements. Application-specific values may be carried using the data methods provided by this class.

    Author:
    Charles B. Kozoyed

    • Constructor Detail

      • Agent

        public Agent()
        Creates a new agent.

        The agent is assigned a unique UUID and creation timestamp. Its protocol is initially Protocol.UNKNOWN, and its serialized size is initially zero.

    • Method Detail

      • setData

        public void setData​(String key,
                    Object value)
        Associates an application-defined value with the specified key.

        The data map provides a dynamic alternative to defining application data as fields in an Agent subclass. A value may be null, but the key must not be null or blank.

        Parameters:
        key - the key used to identify the value
        value - the value to associate with the key; may be null
        Throws:
        IllegalArgumentException - if key is null or blank

      • setData

        public void setData​(Enum<?> key,
                    Object value)
        Associates an application-defined value with the name of the specified enum constant.

        The key may be a constant from any enum type. The enum constant's Enum.name() is used as the data key. Using an enum key provides compile-time checking and helps prevent errors caused by mistyped string keys. A value may be null.

        Parameters:
        key - an enum constant whose name is used as the data key
        value - the value to associate with the key; may be null
        Throws:
        IllegalArgumentException - if key is null

      • getData

        public <T> T getData​(Enum<?> key,
                     Class<T> clazz)
        Returns the value associated with the name of the specified enum constant.

        The key may be a constant from any enum type. The enum constant's Enum.name() is used as the data key. The value is returned as the requested type. A stored null value is returned as null. Using an enum key provides compile-time checking and helps prevent errors caused by mistyped string keys.

        Type Parameters:
        T - the expected type of the value
        Parameters:
        key - an enum constant whose name is used as the data key
        clazz - the expected type of the value
        Returns:
        the value associated with the key, or null if the stored value is null
        Throws:
        IllegalArgumentException - if key or clazz is null
        IllegalStateException - if no data is present, the key does not exist, or the value is not of the requested type

      • hasData

        public boolean hasData​(Enum<?> key)
        Determines whether data is associated with the name of the specified enum constant.

        The key may be a constant from any enum type. The enum constant's Enum.name() is used as the data key. This method returns true even if the value associated with the key is null. Using an enum key provides compile-time checking and helps prevent errors caused by mistyped string keys.

        Parameters:
        key - an enum constant whose name is used as the data key
        Returns:
        true if the key exists; otherwise false
        Throws:
        IllegalArgumentException - if key is null

      • getCreationTimeStamp

        public long getCreationTimeStamp()
        Returns the agent creation timestamp.

      • getLatencyRecord

        public LatencyRecord getLatencyRecord()
        Returns the latency record associated with this agent.

        The latency record contains timing information collected during agent communication and processing. Advanced users may inspect the associated LatencyContext and LatencyMetric values to analyze individual processing stages.

        Latency information may be unavailable if metrics collection is disabled or the record has not been initialized.

        Returns:
        the latency record associated with this agent, or null if no record is available
        See Also:
        LatencyRecord, LatencyContext, LatencyMetric

      • getProtocol

        public Protocol getProtocol()
        Obtain the value of the protocol for this communications entity. This method retrieves the current protocol being used by the communications entity, which may be important for understanding the type of communication and its capabilities. The protocol could influence aspects such as security, data format, and transmission methods.
        Returns:
        The current protocol being used, represented as a Protocol object.

      • setVisitMethod

        public void setVisitMethod​(String visitorMethodName,
                           Class apiClass)
        Sets the visit method name and API class for the visitor. This specifies the method that will be called on the receiver when it interacts with the receiver. It specifies this be supplying the method name and the one and only parameter the API (apiClass) that is injected into the agent.
        Parameters:
        visitorMethodName - The name of the visit method.
        apiClass - The class of the API that the visit method belongs to.
        Throws:
        IllegalArgumentException - if the visitorMethodName or apiClass is null.

      • setVisitMethod

        public void setVisitMethod​(String visitorMethodName,
                           String apiClassName)
        Sets the visit method name and API class for the visitor. This specifies the method that will be called on the receiver when it interacts with the receiver. It specifies this be supplying the method name and the one and only parameter the API (apiClass) that is injected into the agent.
        Parameters:
        visitorMethodName - the name of the visit method; must not be null.
        apiClassName - the name of the API class; must not be null.
        Throws:
        IllegalArgumentException - if either the visitorMethodName or apiClassName is null.

      • toLogString

        public String toLogString​(String logLine)
        Returns a string representation of the current object, which includes the name of the class, the visitor method name, and the API class name. If the visitor method name or API class name is null, it will be represented as "null". The API class name is extracted from its fully qualified name, retaining only the simple class name.
        Parameters:
        logLine - the message to include in the log string
        Returns:
        a string in the format agent=<class name> method=<visitor method> api=<api class name>
